revision.title: Trust and Security Assessment Framework for Agentic DeFi
revision.summary: Owney turns its Trust and Security Assessment Framework for DeFi agents (13 subcategories, 3 platforms assessed) into an open, machine-readable standard and a continuous assessment pipeline that agent platforms integrate with. Today no independent, public, versioned assessment tells depositors which agents are safe to use.

sections.why:
Autonomous agents move user liquidity across DeFi on Ethereum and its L2s. A model, a prompt, a hot key, an operator, every protocol touched: any one can lose the funds. Depositors (individuals and institutions) cannot tell a careful agent from a reckless one.

No agent has lost user funds yet. But during the KelpDAO rsETH exploit (April 2026, $124 million to $230 million of bad debt on Aave) and the Resolv USR depeg (March 2026, about $25 million extracted), Zyfai's agents exited early while depositors sat frozen in Aave (sources: https://www.bankless.com/read/agents-and-x402-make-defi-safer, https://x.com/Zyfai_/status/2036119040528375853). The same autonomy loses funds when screening, key management or incident response is weak. Afterwards, anyone can open the public board and see a current assessment of every integrated agent, re-checked at least every 14 days.
sections.in_scope:
The board exists; this is not a website. The money buys:

- Framework v2: criteria, evidence and scoring for every subcategory, as an open specification plus agent skills a pipeline can execute, and a performance pillar: one reporting format in place of self-reported APY, one metric combining returns with risk.
- A continuous pipeline: platforms integrate once, re-assessment runs on a schedule and on change.
- Re-assessing the 3 existing platforms and onboarding new ones.
sections.out_scope:
- Building or operating any DeFi agent
- Audits of any protocols
- A returns leaderboard: the board never ranks agents by APY
- A heavy platform build

sections.why_grant: Framework v1 is finished: Security, Risk and Robustness, 13 subcategories, a 0 to 10 score on cited evidence. Zyfai, SurfLiquid and Yield Seeker are assessed, results at https://risk.owney.app/, and all three endorsed it publicly. The methodology is still private; publishing it is milestone 1. Rebuilding from scratch would take most of the grant.
sections.commitments:
- OSI-approved license for the specification, skills and pipeline code; methodology public and versioned.
- Re-assessment at least every 14 days and on every reported change; stale assessments marked stale.
- Identical fees, process and criteria for every platform; conflict-of-interest rules published.
- Owney maintains it after the grant, funded by fees from connected platforms and assessment work.
- Pinned targets: 6 platforms assessed, 3 integrated with over $200,000 of user funds each.

milestones.name: Framework v2, formalized for machine processing
criteria: Framework v2 (13 subcategories plus a performance pillar based on the AtlasYield KPIs) published under an OSI-approved license with a dated changelog
Skills in a public repository; the 3 existing platforms re-assessed with v2, live on the board with the version stated

milestones.name: Continuous assessment pipeline for agent integration
criteria: Integration documentation, conflict-of-interest rules and fee schedule published
At least 3 platforms re-assessed by the pipeline without manual intervention, results on the board with version and date

milestones.name: Adoption evidence
criteria: At least 6 DeFi agent platforms assessed with v2 and live on the board

At least 3 agent platforms outside Owney, running on Ethereum or an Ethereum L2, integrated with the pipeline, each managing over $200,000 of user funds and together over $5,000,000, measured onchain with the query linked, re-assessment history live on the board

At least 3 platforms change their setup to fix a finding from their assessment (key management, screening or incident response), shown in the re-assessment history on the board and confirmed by the independent technical reviewer
A public metrics page and the maintenance and funding plan published with a named maintainer
At least $3,000 of assessment or pipeline fees collected from connected platforms, not counting grants, confirmed by the independent technical reviewer
